check_description:
This check verifies that `market_model.xlsx` includes at least three named cage-ban transition scenarios spanning the realistic range of how the colony cohort exits by end-2027, with pricing per system varying across scenarios rather than held flat.
All of: (a) At least three named scenarios present. (b) Scenarios span the realistic range from successful end-2027 transition through material slippage / oversupply, not clustered around a single outcome. (c) Pricing per system (free-range vs barn vs colony) varies across scenarios; at minimum the free-range-premium compression path differs and barn pricing reflects supply pressure under at least one scenario.
score_0_criteria: Fewer than 3 named scenarios; or scenarios are clustered (all show similar outcomes); or pricing is held flat across scenarios with only volume / capacity differences (a 'point-estimate forecast that ignores supply pricing dynamics' per standards 3.1).
score_1_criteria: All three: >=3 named scenarios (e.g., 'Managed Conversion' / 'Capacity Gap' / 'Premium Collapse'); scenarios span the range of outcomes from successful end-2027 transition through to material slippage / oversupply; and price trajectory varies across scenarios; at minimum the free-range premium compression path differs across scenarios (e.g., central 18->14->12%, downside 18->12->8%, upside 18->16->14%) and barn pricing reflects supply pressure under at least one scenario. Per standards Section 3.1: 'When supply expands faster than demand, the price tier most exposed must show compression. Models that hold prices flat across supply scenarios are flagged as deficient.'
specific_file_locations:
nz_supermarkets_cagefree_commitments_summary.pdf: 'Foodstuffs ... has committed to packaged shell eggs being sourced exclusively from cage-free production by the end of 2027.' Woolworths NZ 'indicated that its packaged shell-egg range is already cage-free on shelf'. The combined Foodstuffs + Woolworths NZ duopoly functions as a 'de-facto industry deadline for shell-egg producers carrying meaningful colony-cage exposure'.

transcript_industry_expert_part3.pdf [00:10:38-00:13:00]: 'FY26 averages 18% premium for free-range over barn at the wholesale gate. FY27 - as the bulk of Phase 2 barn capacity comes online ahead of the deadline - drops to 14%. FY28 - post-deadline, when barn supply has fully stood up - settles at 12%.' Plus downside: 'Premium goes to 8-10% by FY28 if barn supply oversteps demand and you get a price war on the free-range tier.' Plus upside: 'the trajectory stabilises at 14-15% FY28 if some marginal barn capacity doesn't come online and supply stays tight.'

transcript_industry_expert_part2.pdf [00:08:22-00:08:30]: 'End-2027 deadline is 19 months away from now. So if the McKenna business haven't started consents yet, they're behind.' Plus: 'They needed to be in market for consents by Q4 last year to be comfortable. By now, if they haven't lodged, they're scraping.'

halberd_analytical_standards.docx Section 3.1: 'For supply-driven scenarios in commodity / quasi-commodity markets, the price response must be modeled, not held flat. When supply expands faster than demand, the price tier most exposed must show compression. Models that hold prices flat across supply scenarios are flagged as deficient.'

At least 3 named scenarios required.

check_description:
This check verifies that `market_model.xlsx` (a) sizes Aurora as net-additive to the public producer roster, (b) includes >=3 named cage-ban transition scenarios with distinct drivers, (c) differentiates cage-free conversion timing per named producer, and (d) differentiates the free-range-over-barn premium trajectory across scenarios.
All of: (a) Aurora sized at source-anchored flock count or volume share equivalent and added net-additive to the public roster (bottom-up roster sums above published industry total by Aurora's contribution, or commentary explicitly confirms additive treatment). (b) >=3 named scenarios with distinct drivers. Three variations of the same case do not satisfy. (c) Per-producer cage-free progress differentiated across leader / laggard / mid-pack. Single industry-wide % applied uniformly fails. (d) free-range-over-barn premium trajectory differs across scenarios with central, downside, and upside paths visibly distinct. Same free-range curve across all scenarios fails.
score_0_criteria: Any of: Aurora cannibalised from existing producers' shares (bottom-up roster sums to or below the published industry total without Aurora's net contribution); or Aurora sized materially outside 600-650k bird range without source justification; or fewer than three named transition scenarios; or scenarios are unnamed / point-estimate / ignore the 2027 retailer pledge; or scenarios share drivers (e.g. three variations of the same managed-conversion case); or conversion timing applied uniformly to all producers (no leader / laggard differentiation across Mainland / Heyden / Aurora); or free-range premium trajectory held constant across scenarios (only volume / share varies, free-range premium curve identical in every scenario).

Aurora has to be added on top of the publicly tracked roster'; and (b) at least three named cage-ban transition scenarios with distinct drivers per scenario (e.g. managed-conversion vs capacity-gap vs premium-collapse, or equivalent named scenario set spanning the realistic forward range); and (c) per-producer cage-free conversion progress is differentiated; Mainland identified as leader (~80-85%), Heyden as laggard (~45-50%), Aurora at ~40% colony exposure with end-2027 deadline; per Calthorpe Part 1 [00:16:22] 'Mainland was already mostly cage-free pre-Phase-2 ... roughly 80% cage-free now, finishing out the remaining 20% over the next 18 months. Aurora at 60% cage-free - 30% barn plus 30% free-range - is in the middle of the pack but with the largest single-block of colony to convert' (or equivalent producer-level granularity that distinguishes leaders from laggards rather than applying a single industry-wide conversion % uniformly); and (d) the free-range-over-barn premium trajectory differs across scenarios with at least the central (~18->14->12%), downside (~8-10% FY28), and upside (~14-15% FY28) paths visibly distinct.

check_description:
This check verifies that financial figures in `market_model.xlsx` follow Halberd's firm-wide convention: presented in USD with FX rates drawn from the firm's central financial assumptions workbook (not spot rates from external sources / training data, not a flat rate across multi-year cash flows).
All of: (a) Financial figures presented in USD (not native NZD / AUD only). Acceptable: USD-only or local + USD side-by-side. (b) FX rate(s) applied are documented (footnote, sheet note, slide footer, or narration) with citation to the firm's central financial assumptions workbook and the FY-aligned rate used. (c) For multi-year cash flows, forecast rates by year applied (not flat spot) where the workbook provides such rates.
If the deliverable contains no financial figures (e.g. only % volume share), the check is satisfied by default.
score_0_criteria: Output presents financial figures only in native local currency (NZD / AUD / etc.) without USD conversion, or converts to USD but uses an unsourced spot rate / training-data rate without documenting the workbook + FY-aligned rate, or uses a flat spot rate across multi-year cash flows where forecast rates by year were available in the workbook. Specific failure modes include: (a) uses an NZD/USD rate outside the 0.58-0.66 historical band (likely a training-data spot or stale rate); (b) uses a flat rate across multi-year cash flows (e.g., 0.585 applied to all of FY25-FY30); (c) cites a single rate without documenting which workbook FY-year it corresponds to.
score_1_criteria:
Output presents financial figures in USD and documents the FX rate(s) applied with citation to halberd_central_financial_assumptions.xlsx (per the Notes tab directive: 'All Halberd deal-team financial outputs (memos, models, decks, briefings) are presented in USD' and 'Do not use spot rates from external sources or training data', and the FX_Rates_Forecast tab directive: 'Apply forecast rates by year for multi-year cash flows. Do not use a flat spot rate.'). Acceptable forms: (a) explicit USD-only presentation with a footnote / sheet note / slide footer naming the workbook and the FY-rate used; (b) as-stated local + USD-converted side-by-side with the same documentation; (c) for outputs with no financial figures, the check is satisfied by default.

The workbook FX_Rates_Historical and FX_Rates_Forecast tabs carry these NZD/USD rates (USD per 1 unit NZD):

Historical: FY2022 0.654; FY2023 0.625; FY2024 0.602; FY2025 0.585.
Forecast (Halberd Macro Strategy Group, April 2026 update): FY2026 0.595; FY2027 0.610; FY2028 0.620; FY2029 0.625; FY2030 0.625; FY2031 0.625.

For the W1-T2 5-year forecast horizon (FY25 actual + FY26-FY30 forecast), the model should apply the per-year curve 0.585 (FY25) / 0.595 (FY26) / 0.610 (FY27) / 0.620 (FY28) / 0.625 (FY29) / 0.625 (FY30) - not a flat spot rate. Historical FY24 figures convert at 0.602.

Acceptable tolerance: per-year rate within +-0.005 of the workbook value (rounding to 3 decimal places is fine). A flat single-rate applied across all years - even if the rate value matches one workbook year - fails the multi-year-curve requirement.
specific_file_locations:
halberd_central_financial_assumptions.xlsx Notes tab states (in full): '1. Currency of report: All Halberd deal-team financial outputs (memos, models, decks, briefings) are presented in USD. Where source materials carry local-currency figures (NZD, AUD, etc.), apply the rates in this workbook to convert. Do not use spot rates from external sources or training data.'

FX_Rates_Forecast tab (Halberd Macro Strategy Group, April 2026 update) carries NZD/USD forecast rates: FY2026 0.595; FY2027 0.610; FY2028 0.620; FY2029 0.625; FY2030 0.625; FY2031 0.625.

Convention is firm-wide and is not restated in the task description or any other internal Halberd document; discovery requires reading the assumptions workbook.

check_description:
This check verifies that the forecast in `market_model.xlsx` quantifies both (a) dietary-mix shift as an explicit per-capita driver and (b) plant-based substitution sensitivity as a downside risk to forward egg demand.
All of: (a) Dietary-mix shift (flexitarian / vegetarian) is an explicit forecast driver adding the source-anchored uplift to per-capita egg consumption, sourced from the dietary-trends survey or equivalent. (b) Plant-based substitution sensitivity surfaced; acceptable forms: a scenario lever; or a sensitivity table; or an explicit downside narrative anchored in the expert interview series and the dietary-trends egg-substitute addendum.
score_0_criteria: Any of: dietary-mix shift not used as a forecast driver (per-capita modelled flat or declining without dietary uplift); or dietary-mix used at materially wrong magnitude (below 0.2% or above 0.8% pa without source justification); or plant-based substitution sensitivity not surfaced; or plant-based treated as immaterial without engaging the Calthorpe Part 5 / ACII addendum evidence.

ACII: 'Combined, the segment-mix shift adds approximately 0.4-0.6% per year to per-capita egg consumption, before accounting for population growth'); and (b) plant-based substitution sensitivity is surfaced; either as a scenario lever, a sensitivity table, or an explicit downside narrative anchored in the consumer research / Calthorpe Part 5 evidence base (per Calthorpe Part 5: 'a sensitivity scenario where 1.5 to 2.5% of national shell-egg volume is displaced by plant-based product').

check_description:
This check verifies that `market_model.xlsx` applies the cross-channel pricing discipline mandated by the firm's analytical standards: at least three distinct channel price levels and a two-column retail structure, applying the standards-aligned gross-margin / markup-factor convention.
All of: (a) Three distinct channel price levels: retail wholesale, foodservice, industrial (and direct if modelled) each carry separate prices. (b) Two-column retail structure: retail wholesale and retail at-shelf as separate columns, not collapsed into a single 'retail price' field. (c) Standards-aligned uplift applied (either as gross margin or as markup factor from shelf to gate). Subtracting a flat gross-margin % from shelf to derive gate (produces wrong/lower wholesale figure) fails. (d) Multiplier documented in a labelled Assumptions cell with source attribution to the firm's analytical standards and convention used. Note on current firm authority: the v3.8 analytical standards document is stale (Q2 2024, pending v4.2 refresh); per Hugh Pemberton's pin in general/2026-04-22.json the current authority for any directive updated in Slack is the Slack guidance. The markup-factor convention is reinforced by Vivian Holst in deal/2026-05-05.json (ts 1778014920): multiplicative 1.33-1.54 (or divide shelf by 1.33-1.54), not a flat subtraction.
score_0_criteria: Any of: (a) single blended retail price across channels; (b) retail wholesale and shelf collapsed into one column; (c) flat 25-35% subtracted from shelf to derive wholesale (produces the wrong gate figure; the wrong convention conflates gross margin % with markup factor); (d) multiplier is hardcoded / unlabelled / has no source attribution.
score_1_criteria: All four: (a) three distinct channel prices; (b) two-column retail (wholesale + shelf); (c) standards-aligned uplift via either 25-35% gross-margin-from-wholesale or 1.33-1.54 markup-factor-from-shelf; per standards 2.3: 'When deriving wholesale gate from scan-data shelf prices, divide by the 1.33-1.54 markup factor; do not subtract a flat 25-35% from shelf, which produces a different (and lower) wholesale figure'; (d) multiplier documented in a labelled Assumptions cell with source attribution.
specific_file_locations:
halberd_analytical_standards.docx Section 2.3 (updated): 'The retailer's gross margin (shelf-minus-gate / shelf) typically sits at 25-35%, which is the firm's working anchor. Equivalently, the shelf-over-gate markup factor is approximately 1.33-1.54 (a wholesale gate of $X maps to a shelf of $Y where Y/X = 1.33-1.54). When deriving wholesale gate from scan-data shelf prices, divide by the 1.33-1.54 markup factor; do not subtract a flat 25-35% from shelf, which produces a different (and lower) wholesale figure.'

Original Section 2.3 text: 'Different channels carry different unit economics. Models that apply a single blended wholesale price across all channels under-state revenue dispersion and miss the value-pool concentration risk. Required treatment: Retail wholesale price separate from retail shelf price - apply the channel uplift (typically 25-35%) explicitly; Foodservice gate price separate from retail wholesale (typically 10-15% below retail wholesale); Industrial / processor gate price separate from foodservice (typically 30-45% below retail wholesale); Direct / DTC price band separate (typically 40-60% above retail shelf for premium-tier direct).'

transcript_industry_expert_part1.pdf [00:05:38] confirms 4-channel structure with different unit economics.

transcript_industry_expert_part3.pdf [00:03:42] details industrial bulk pricing vs foodservice distributor margin vs retail markup.

shared/slack_export_halberd/albatross-deal/2026-05-05.json (U002 Vivian Holst, ts 1778014920, current firm authority on the markup-factor convention per the v3.8 -> v4.2 Slack-pin protocol). Per Managing Partner pin in general/2026-04-22.json (Hugh Pemberton, ts 1776869400): 'where my recent guidance in the deal-team channels has updated a directive that v3.8 covers, treat the Slack guidance as the current firm view'. The v3.8 standards section remains the underlying directive; the Slack carrier below is the current authority. Verbatim Vivian Holst directive: 'Theo - no, that's the wrong convention and it'll come back at us. Shelf-over-gate is a markup factor, not a gross-margin subtraction. Apply the factor 1.33-1.54 to gate to get shelf; equivalently, divide shelf by 1.33-1.54 to back out the implied wholesale. Subtracting a flat 25-35% from shelf is a different number and a lower one - the firm view is the markup-factor form for the scan-data-backwards step. The principle is multiplicative, not additive.' This Slack carrier confirms the markup-factor convention is the current firm view (multiplicative 1.33-1.54 applied to gate, or shelf divided by 1.33-1.54 to back out wholesale); subtracting a flat 25-35% gross-margin from shelf is explicitly the wrong convention and produces a different (lower) wholesale figure. The exchange is triggered by Theo (U006) asking 'For the retail wholesale gate I'm taking the scan-data shelf price and subtracting 30% to back out the wholesale figure. Sound right?' (ts 1778014800), and Theo acknowledging the correction at ts 1778014980 with 'Redoing with /1.33-1.54 on the scan-data shelf side. Will document the convention in the assumptions tab.'

check_description:
This check verifies both render integrity and assumption traceability in `market_model.xlsx` (no broken cells, no truncation, descriptive tab names, no formula text, and every key input on the Assumptions tab carries both a source-file attribution and a date / vintage annotation) and the workbook formatting convention mandated by the firm's analytical standards (at least four visually distinguishable cell categories, applied consistently across all tabs, with a plain-language legend).

All of: (a) No error values in any populated cell. (b) No truncation in any tab the deal team would inspect. (c) Tabs named with descriptive labels, not default Excel sheet names. (d) Cells where formulas were intended produce values, not literal text. (e) Assumptions tab presents every key input with explicit source-file attribution column (or per-cell source comment / sheet note); orphan inputs fail; missing Assumptions tab fails. (f) Every key input also carries a date / vintage annotation. Source filename without any vintage indicator fails. May be combined with attribution column. (g) At least four cell categories carry visually distinguishable treatments. Distinguishable by font colour, fill colour, bold, border, or any combination. (h) Treatment for each category applied consistently across every tab where that category appears.
- (i) Legend present in the workbook: dedicated tab or clearly labelled block within the Assumptions tab; legend names each category and its visual treatment in plain language.

Reasonable category names acceptable; additional categories acceptable. Default Excel formatting automatically fails. Note on current firm authority: the v3.8 analytical standards document is stale (Q2 2024, pending v4.2 refresh); per Hugh Pemberton's pin in general/2026-04-22.json the current authority for any directive updated in Slack is the Slack guidance. The cell formatting convention (>=4 visually distinguishable categories + consistent treatment across all tabs + plain-language legend) is reinforced by Daniel Reyes in deal/2026-05-04.json (ts 1777898520) at the start of the model build.
score_0_criteria: Any of: (a) cell shows '#REF!' / '#DIV/0!' / '#name?' / '#value!' (or other formula errors); or (b) any column displays '###' from truncation in a tab the deal team would normally view; or (c) any tab retains the default 'Sheet1' / 'Sheet2' / 'Sheet3' naming; or (d) cells where formulas were intended display the formula text literally (e.g., '=SUM(A1:A10)' as text instead of evaluating); or (e) Assumptions tab lacks a source-attribution column / per-cell source notes; or multiple input cells have no traceable source (orphans); or Assumptions tab is missing entirely; or (f) inputs list only a source name / filename without any date / vintage annotation (publication date or interview date); or vintage is shown for only a subset of inputs while others are vintage-less; or (g) fewer than 4 visually distinguishable cell categories; e.g., assumption cells and calculation cells share the same default font colour and fill, or only 2-3 categories are differentiated; or (h) treatment is inconsistent across tabs; e.g., assumption cells are blue in the Assumptions tab but plain black elsewhere, or formulas are highlighted in one tab and not in others; or (i) no legend is present anywhere in the workbook explaining the convention; or a 'legend' exists but does not name each category and its visual treatment in plain language (e.g., a single coloured cell with no label); or the workbook ships with the default Excel formatting (everything black on white, no distinction between hardcoded and calculated cells).

check_description:
This check verifies that `market_model.xlsx` (including any narrative tabs, notes, headers, or commentary cells) complies with two firm-wide Halberd conventions: (a) the no-recommendation rule, and (b) US English spelling.

The deliverable must verify all of:
(a) No explicit invest / pass / continue-diligence recommendation language and no thesis-pillar framing in any cell, tab, or comment. The rule is firm-wide per standards Section 9 and IC pre-read template Section 4 Hard Rules; both sources prohibit a recommendation position in any preliminary deliverable.
(b) US English spelling across every authored-prose cell in the workbook: tab names, header strings, comment cells, and the Notes / Assumptions / Sources tab prose. Numbers and formulas are not in scope. Halberd is a US private-equity firm; US English is the implicit firm-wide convention. Any single instance of British / Commonwealth spelling fails this sub-criterion - e.g., 'realise' instead of 'realize', 'organise', 'colour', 'centre', 'programme', 'analyse', 'favour', 'behaviour', 'specialise'. Proper-noun spellings retain their canonical form (e.g., 'World Organisation for Animal Health' / WOAH, registered company names, official department names) and do not count as fails.

All sub-criteria must pass; failure on any one fails the check.
score_0_criteria: Any of: (a) explicit recommendation phrase present in any cell, header, or note ('we recommend invest', 'we recommend pass', 'continue diligence', 'we should proceed', 'bid at X', equivalent); or thesis-pillar framing present as a structural element (tab name, header, callout, or summary cell using 'compelling opportunity' / 'attractive asset' / 'strong fit for the platform' / equivalent thesis-style framing); or (b) any single instance of British or Commonwealth spelling in any authored-prose cell of the workbook (excluding proper nouns / registered org names; numbers and formulas out of scope) - e.g., realise, organise, colour, centre, programme, analyse, favour, behaviour, specialise, kilometre, defence, licence (when used as a verb); one instance is enough to fail.
score_1_criteria: All of: (a) no explicit invest / pass / continue-diligence recommendation language and no thesis-pillar / 'compelling fit' / 'attractive opportunity' / 'strong platform fit' framing as a structural element in any tab, header, cell, or commentary block in `market_model.xlsx`; neutral descriptive use of words like 'attractive' embedded in commentary (e.g. 'attractive entry multiple') is acceptable provided it is not framed as a thesis pillar; (b) every authored-prose cell in the workbook (tab names, headers, comments, Notes / Assumptions / Sources tab prose) uses US English spelling; proper nouns and registered organisation names retain canonical spelling and do not count as fails; numbers and formulas are not in scope.

check_description:
Pairwise: which `market_model.xlsx` is the stronger Excel market-sizing and cage-ban transition workbook on quality dimensions distinct from the binary A/C checks?
Four dimensions:
- (1) Methodology transparency: intermediate calculations are formula-driven and auditable; flock x eggs/hen x utilisation x channel-weighted prices and any scenario flexing are visible cell-by-cell rather than collapsed into hard-coded results. Magic numbers without a derivable trail count against the workbook.
- (2) Assumption surfacing: a dedicated Assumptions tab (or clearly labelled assumption block) presents key inputs in one place with a source-and-vintage column. A reviewer can find every driver input without navigating multiple tabs.
- (3) Scenario / sensitivity clarity: scenarios are presented in parallel structure with clearly named driver inputs; flexing a scenario driver (e.g. cage-ban transition pace, free-range premium path, feed-grain shock) visibly propagates through dependent cells rather than each scenario being a static snapshot.
- (4) Reconciliation discipline: the top-down vs bottom-up gap is explicitly surfaced and discussed with the gap quantified (e.g. ~19% non-retail channel coverage) rather than silently averaged, blended, or normalised away.
A stronger workbook addresses all four dimensions with formula-driven cells and visible commentary. Apparent depth (more tabs, more rows) does not satisfy the dimensions unless the substantive analytical content is present. Note on current firm authority: the v3.8 analytical standards document is stale (Q2 2024, pending v4.2 refresh); per Hugh Pemberton's pin in general/2026-04-22.json the current authority for any directive updated in Slack is the Slack guidance. The source-and-vintage attribution requirement (dimension 2) is reinforced by Iris Beaumont in admin/2026-05-05.json (ts 1778011200).
score_0_criteria: Output B is stronger across the same four dimensions (or strictly stronger on at least one with no regression). Pairwise: which `market_model.xlsx` is the more polished, professional Excel market-sizing workbook across four XLSX-specific presentation dimensions?
Four dimensions:
- (1) Workbook integrity: no error values (#REF!, #DIV/0!, #VALUE!, #NAME?, #N/A) in any populated cell; the workbook opens in fresh Excel / LibreOffice without recalculation errors or broken cross-sheet references.
- (2) Tab organisation and naming: tabs follow a sensible logical sequence (e.g. historical -> forecast -> scenarios -> assumptions, or equivalent); no default 'Sheet1' / 'Sheet2' names; no empty or placeholder tabs.
- (3) Number formatting and column hygiene: NZ$M / USD / % / decimal places are consistent within columns; column widths are sufficient (no '###' truncation; no zero-width columns hiding content); merged-cell content does not overflow or overlap; headers are readable.
- (4) Cross-sheet linkage: scenario tabs and the assumptions tab are linked by formula references rather than copy-pasted values; flexing an assumption propagates to the dependent scenario / output cells.
A stronger output is more polished across the four dimensions. Surface size (more rows, more tabs) is not polish; broken formulas or error cells in either output are an automatic loss on the workbook-integrity dimension.
